title: Manthey marks 30 years with two sharper Porsche race cars
extract: Manthey has revealed anniversary versions of the Porsche 911 GT3 Cup and 718 Cayman GT4 RS Clubsport. The 911 gains a 4.2-litre flat-six producing 552 hp, revised cooling and aerodynamics, while both track-focused cars are limited to 15 examples each.

title: Porsche teases an 8,000-rpm redline for its Mission S supercar concept
extract: Porsche has shown the Mission S concept's animated gauge cluster, with a tachometer approaching an 8,000-rpm redline. The powertrain remains unconfirmed, but the planned October 15 reveal could preview a new range-topping performance car.

title: Honda's next hybrid system promises better handling and electric all-wheel drive
extract: Honda has outlined a next-generation hybrid platform with improved efficiency, lighter and more rigid vehicle structures, a new Motion Management System and electric all-wheel drive. The company says it aims to improve driver engagement as well as fuel economy.

title: Stack Overflow survey finds developers use AI heavily but still distrust its answers
extract: Stack Overflow's survey of 30,903 developers found AI tools are routine for many respondents, yet only around 7 percent trust AI output for important work decisions. Source attribution matters to 79 percent, underlining the need to verify generated code and technical advice.

title: GitHub is rebuilding its Git storage architecture to handle the agent boom
extract: GitHub is redesigning repository storage as coding agents drive a sharp increase in traffic. Early internal tests reportedly show a 35-fold improvement in write performance, with separate read and write paths and maintenance moved out of the serving path.

title: Study finds AI coding agents produce more code, but not necessarily more software
extract: A study drawing on engineering activity across more than 700,000 employees found that faster AI-assisted coding can be offset by longer review cycles and more revisions. The researchers found little evidence so far that these tools consistently increase overall software output or reduce employment.

title: Alan Turing Institute chief calls for UK control over critical AI capabilities
extract: George Williamson, the new head of the Alan Turing Institute, argues that the UK should not depend entirely on AI systems controlled abroad. He says domestic capability matters for national resilience because access to foreign systems can be restricted by political or commercial decisions.

title: Geargrafx emulator adds automatic overscan cropping and CRT aspect-ratio support
extract: The open-source TurboGrafx-16 and PC Engine emulator has added automatic overscan cropping and CRT aspect-ratio handling. Other recent commits also address save-state compatibility and a timer-underflow bug, improving accuracy and reliability on modern displays.

title: OpenRCT2 v0.5.6 brings land recolouring and a new title sequence
extract: The latest OpenRCT2 release adds recolourable land surfaces and edges, 18 additional colours including five from the original RollerCoaster Tycoon, a new title sequence and improvements to track design and park management.

title: Yiyun Li reflects on Anne Carson's Nobel recognition and life-sustaining writing
extract: Following Anne Carson's Nobel Prize in Literature, novelist Yiyun Li reflects on Carson's singular approach to language and her translations of Euripides. Li describes returning to Carson's work during profound personal grief and explains why the recognition feels both joyful and deserved.

title: Author AK Blakemore discusses the books that shaped her writing
extract: The novelist and poet talks about formative encounters with The Great Gatsby, Orlando and other books, including works she has changed her mind about. The conversation also points readers towards her new novel, Doom Painting, and contemporary fiction she has recently admired.

title: Ray Gunn review: Brad Bird brings old-school film noir to animated science fiction
extract: Brad Bird's new animated film combines a retro-futurist city, hard-boiled detective fiction and a cast led by Sam Rockwell, Tom Waits and Scarlett Johansson. The review praises its imaginative visual design, humour and old-fashioned storytelling, with echoes of Metropolis and Blade Runner.

title: The Guardian's weekly guide to new films, television, games and stage shows
extract: The week's entertainment guide previews Aaron Sorkin's The Social Reckoning, Paul Greengrass's historical drama The Uprising, new streaming adaptations, Marvel's VisionQuest and several stage and comedy events. It rounds up upcoming film, television, game and theatre releases.
